title: Test Suite Counterpart to checkmate
text: Suppose R package defines function. Perhaps already added {checkmate} assertions, perhaps test function inputs way. case, assume function looks like : cover unit tests, ’d normally * test invariants, * test function behaviour valid arguments, * test errors raised invalid arguments. last part usually tedious - parameter function, test different values, failing different reason. example, ’d need test column given NULL, non-character value, empty character vector, character vector length 2+, empty string, NA_character_, etc. end involving lot copying pasting, even consider issue coding LLM, real problem remains: tests supposed define requirements function/parameter behaviour, reading tedious ’s easy miss test case somewhere. Instead, use {gambit} specify tests (called “needs”) just like ’d specify {checkmate} assertions. generate several snapshots use `testthat::expect_snapshot() hood: gambit specification requires parameter name (e.g. "column") example valid function call (e.g. move_rook("", 3L, direction = "")), parameters analogues {checkmate} parameters (except using underscores instead dots). Additionally, {gambit} makes additional assertions needs specifications, allowing - example - specify n_chars min_chars simultaneously. Note function provide never supposed execute entirety, execution time never come play, assertions come first. fact, note none exceptions mention board move_rook() uses definition, even though hasn’t defined anywhere. ’s never get far.
